title: Britannia Industries Ltd - 500825 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Britannia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to INR 5,542 crore, with PAT at 13% of revenue and H1 revenue crossing INR 10,000 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 5,542 crore, up 16.6% YoY and 11.6% QoQ, with PAT up 10.2% YoY and 13% margin on revenue. H1 revenue was INR 10,506 crore (up 13.1%), the first time H1 crossed INR 10,000 crore. Volume growth was 13% on a low base of minus 3%, and General Trade (GT) accelerated, with management attributing part of this to a GST transition base effect worth 1.5-2%. Input costs (wheat flour, palm oil, sugar, milk, laminate, fuel) rose sharply YoY, and a 3.5% price increase was implemented in the quarter with more in the pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: Growth as stated 8.5% YoY; management cited operating profit margin around 17%

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: GT growth in Q2 FY27 is 2.6x the full-year FY26 growth rate, per management; GT is the largest part of the business. Growth described as uniform across opportunity and mature states, with rural and semi-urban strong.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce is trending at close to 7% of overall sales (FY26 about 6%); management says it would be in double digits excluding INR 5 pack sales, and the company is treating it as a separate business unit.

segments.name: Other channels (modern trade, alternate, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Growing at a rate significantly above GT, per management.

segments.name: Adjacency bakery business
segments.commentary: Grew more than 20%, led by croissant and cake; rusk growing slower. Dairy: cheese performing better (flavoured slices launched about 1.5 months earlier); Sattvam Ghee and Winkin' Cow milk drink trending well.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Recovered after Q1 disruption from Middle East war; Middle East Africa and rest of International both grew in good double digits, though Middle East costs remain high due to freight premiums.

segments.name: Biscuits share of portfolio
segments.commentary: Biscuits about 78-80% of total sales, with non-biscuit portfolio expected to grow faster.

guidance_outlook: Further price increases (activation/shrinkflation-led) are in the works; the 3.5% taken in the quarter covers only part of cost inflation, and management aims to close the gap with subsequent increases; implementation takes about 1.5-2 months.
Management declined to guide on future gross margin trajectory, saying inflation is expected to persist and events are hard to predict.
Grammage reduction is expected to weigh on volumes going ahead, though management remains confident in the volume growth story.
Future health and protein platforms are in development; no launch timelines given to protect competitive position.
Cost optimisation programmes to continue this year to limit pass-through to consumers.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were discussed in the call.
Renewable electricity share in own plants at 48%, constrained by state government caps on renewable usage.
Women make up 45% of factory workforce; Britannia Nutrition Foundation reached about 5.73 lakh beneficiaries in H1.
demand_pricing: Input costs YoY: wheat flour marginally down; refined palm oil up 17%; sugar up 6%; milk up 16%; laminate up 18%; fuel up 45%. QoQ: wheat flour up 9%, palm oil up 11%, sugar up 4%, milk up 2%, laminate up 7%.
Price increase of 3.5% implemented in Q2; further increases planned. Industry migrated from INR 4.5 fractional pricing to INR 5 and INR 10 price points around May-June 2026.
Management says shelf space has been regained versus Malkist and others after odd-pricing period; NutriChoice Zero growing in strong double digits.

Competition: Malkist (cracker segment, Cheeze Dipped launched by Britannia to compete), and Reliance entering biscuits starting in Tamil Nadu; management says INR 5 and INR 10 price points are harder to disrupt than in cola.
GST-related transition in September last year contributed a base effect of at most 1.5-2% at quarter level.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price increases beyond the 3.5% taken, and how should gross margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3.5% came through, more price increases are in the works, and the 3.5% covers only part of inflation; it declined to predict gross margin direction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GT pickup a base effect or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly base effect (September transition month, impact up to 1.5-2% of quarter), but management also cited resilient GT consumption in semi-urban and rural areas and better own execution; Vipin Kataria said growth is uniform and sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Are you back to pre-odd-pricing market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said Britannia has regained shelf space and share, and the INR 4.5 price point has disappeared from the market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce potential and is it a major growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce at about 7% of sales; management is treating it as a business unit with channel-specific products and sees premiumisation as the key lever; urban e-commerce already in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see wheat coverage and the next crop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Britannia is an efficient wheat buyer, has historically beaten the market with mark-to-market gains, and is watching a challenging monsoon for the next wheat season; no specific coverage percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit vs non-biscuit mix and medium-term growth shape?
qa_highlights.answer: Biscuits are about 78-80% of sales; growth to come from core innovation, higher-margin adjacencies, healthier and Gen Z-targeted products, e-commerce and premiumisation.

risks_watch: Sustained input inflation (palm oil, milk, laminate, sugar, fuel) with only 3.5% price increase so far; gross margin pressure likely to persist.
Volume impact from planned grammage reduction as price increases are taken.
Reliance entry into biscuits starting in Tamil Nadu and fierce competition with Malkist in the cracker segment.
Middle East freight and cost headwinds in International business.
Wheat crop outlook given challenging monsoon; next season's wheat cost.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and volume momentum, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on gross margins, input cost trajectory and future launch timelines, which management withheld citing competition and uncertainty.
key_quotes: Yes, it is a scenario where you are seeing a high level of inflation, and inflation is there to stay.
Obviously, the cost inflation is more than what, and this has only covered part of it.
We have regained our shelf space. We have regained and done better on the share.
Britannia as an organization is extremely bullish on e-commerce.

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance or capacity additions were given; Q2 revenue rose 16.6% YoY on 13% volume growth (low base) and a 3.5% price hike with further increases planned, while management declined to guide on gross margin and said grammage cuts will weigh on volumes ahead.
